what_its_for: Meprobamate is used to help relieve anxiety and tension for short periods of time (usually no longer than 4 months). It works on your brain and nervous system to help you feel calmer and more relaxed.
how_to_take: Take meprobamate exactly as your doctor told you. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food, but if it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a meal or snack. Do not take more than prescribed, and do not take it for longer than your doctor recommends.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 400 mg taken 3 to 4 times a day. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how you respond to the medication. The maximum dose is typically 2,400 mg per day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store meprobamate at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store it in a secure location, out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to safely dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking meprobamate — it can cause dangerous drowsiness and dizziness. Do not drive a car, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medications that cause drowsiness, such as sleep aids, other anti-anxiety medicines, muscle relaxants, or narcotic pain medicines, unless your doctor approves. Do not stop taking meprobamate suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause serious withdrawal symptoms.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: thoughts of harming yourself or suicide, severe allergic reactions (rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, difficulty breathing), extreme confusion or unusual behavior, seizures, very fast or pounding heartbeat, fainting, or severe dizziness. Also contact your doctor if you feel the medication is no longer working, if your anxiety is getting worse, or if you feel you cannot stop taking it.
when_it_works: Meprobamate usually starts working within 1 to 2 hours after you take a dose. Most people feel a calming effect fairly quickly. However, your doctor will re-evaluate whether you still need this medication after about 4 months, since it is not meant for long-term use.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and older): This medication is generally NOT recommended for older adults because it can cause increased confusion, dizziness, and a higher risk of falls. If you are elderly, talk to your doctor about safer alternatives. Pregnancy: Meprobamate may harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: This medication passes into breast milk and may harm a nursing baby. Do not breastfeed while taking meprobamate without talking to your doctor. Children: This medication is not typically recommended for children under 6 years old. Kidney or liver problems: If you have kidney or liver disease, your doctor may need to adjust your dose or choose a different medication for you.
